paperTitle: A Novel Kinect-based Conducting System for Real-time Audiovisual Musical Visualization
centralContribution: This work presents a novel Kinect-based conducting system that utilizes a gestural interface for the real-time audiovisual visualization of complex musical structures, primarily aimed at educational purposes. The system was rigorously evaluated through a user experience (UX) study involving professional conductors, musicians, and users without musical knowledge to validate its viability as a supportive tool for learning conducting and musical theory.

elements.name: Central Contribution
elements.description: A novel Kinect-based conducting system with a gestural interface for real-time audiovisual visualization of complex musical structures, designed for educational purposes and validated through a user experience study.
elements.justification: This is the core innovation and primary objective of the entire paper, as explicitly stated.

elements.name: Abstract Summary
elements.description: There is a need for immersive educational tools to teach conducting without a physical orchestra. Existing interactive conducting systems are often costly or require physical contact. While gestural devices like Kinect offer affordable, contact-free interaction, challenges remain in accurate gesture identification and effective 3D musical visualization. This paper addresses these issues by developing an affordable, interactive, and visually rich Kinect-based system for instrumental conducting education.
elements.justification: This element summarizes the problem context, existing solutions, and the motivation for the paper's contribution, providing a comprehensive overview of the research.

elements.name: Figure 1: System Architecture
elements.description: A diagram illustrating the main components of the Kinect-based conducting system, including the MIDI Processor, Gesture Identifier, Particle System Manager, Kinect device, Unreal Engine, and their interconnections, providing an architectural overview.
elements.justification: This figure is crucial for understanding the fundamental design and interaction of the system's various components, which is central to the paper's methodology.

elements.name: Figure 10: Particle Size and Gesture Path Visualization
elements.description: An animation frame depicting an increase in particle size, directly related to the amplitude of a conductor's gesture, with the real-time path of the gesture also visualized on screen, demonstrating dynamic visual feedback.
elements.justification: This figure visually demonstrates a key aspect of the system's real-time audiovisual mapping, showing how gestural input directly translates into dynamic visual changes and user feedback.

elements.name: Table 2: Average Time per Task by User Group
elements.description: Quantitative results from the User Experience study, showing the average time (in seconds) taken by professional conductors (Group 1), musicians (Group 2), and ordinary users (Group 3) to complete each of the 11 defined tasks.
elements.justification: This table presents the primary quantitative results of the UX study, directly supporting the evaluation of the system's viability and performance across different user groups.

elements.name: Table 3: Median Attempts per Task by User Group
elements.description: Quantitative results showing the median number of attempts required by professional conductors (Group 1), musicians (Group 2), and ordinary users (Group 3) to successfully complete each of the 11 tasks in the User Experience study.
elements.justification: This table provides additional quantitative insights into user performance and task difficulty, complementing the average time data and reinforcing the system's evaluation.

elements.name: Figure 2: Basic Conducting Patterns
elements.description: Diagrams representing four basic conducting patterns (Binary, Ternary, Quaternary, Compound Binary) generated by the authors, which are used as reference gestures for the system's gesture recognition.
elements.justification: This figure introduces the fundamental gestural inputs that the system processes, directly relating to the gesture identification component and the core interaction mechanism.

elements.name: Table 1: User Study Tasks
elements.description: A list of the 11 specific tasks performed by participants in the User Experience study, outlining the gestural controls and musical interactions evaluated.
elements.justification: This table details the experimental setup and the specific actions users performed, providing context for understanding the results presented in Tables 2 and 3.

elements.name: Figure 3: Castel's Color Mapping for Pitch
elements.description: A visual representation of Newton's and Castel's color maps, adapted by the authors, showcasing how different musical pitches are mapped to distinct colors in the 3D scene.
elements.justification: This figure details a specific and important aspect of the system's visual appearance mapping, showing how musical data (pitch) is transformed into visual elements (color), supporting the 'audiovisual visualization' aspect of the contribution.
